pr_body:
This PR is the `master` counterpart of #12457, and fixes #12443.

This is the original message for the 1.1.1 commit:

> ## Fix `d2i_ECPKParameters_fp` and `i2d_ECPKParameters_fp` macroes
>
> These functions are part of the public API but we don't have tests
> covering their usage.
> They are actually implemented as macroes and the absence of tests has
> caused them to fall out-of-sync with the latest changes to ASN1 related
> functions and cause compilation warnings.
>
> This commit fixes the public headers to reflect these changes.

In `master` we inherited the defect in the public header.

The test for this uncovered a second bug, dealing with curves without associated OIDs.
This PR (as well as #12457) also includes a fix for this second issue.

## Tasks

- [x] Cherry-pick test from #12457
- [x] Evaluate if #12443 still affects `master`
  - [x] Fix #12433 in `master` if needed
- [x] Pass `*_fp()` tests in Windows
pr_comments: The fix touches public API, so mandatory OTC decision label added.

Apart from the ongoing discussion on consistency in handling `EC_GROUP_get_asn1_flag()` this PR is now stuck (as #12457 for 1.1.1 has been for the past year) on Windows-specific test failures.

I still have the same questions about these failures:

- are the failures just a peculiarity of our test rigging?
- are the `_fp` variants of our functions supposed to work in Windows?
  - if not, should the prototypes for these functions be masked by some `#ifdef` in the public API?
  - if yes, can we get our testing framework to play nice with whatever needs to happen for these functions to work?
    - if we cannot fix the testing framework, should we disable this specific test for Windows? (what kind of `#ifdef` are rocmmended for this?)
    
I don't like the idea of disabling the test in Windows: if those functions are supposed to work in a Windows environment.
It feels like cheating, and the lack of testing of these functions is what made #12443 possible in the first place.
The last two commits do not change any code, and are just there as a remainder about fixing the typos in the commit messages when merging.

> @levitte can you check if [d1202e8](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/d1202e8e18517f39f765e4ae6da1b6a717631a29) is OK or if I need to tweak it differently?
> The original implementation for 1.1.1 was by @bernd-edlinger but in `master` things changed quite a bit so I had to get creative in my copypaste from `apps/build.info`.
> 
> One thought I had ( which maybe won't work because this whole windows workaround remains a misery to me) was to instead incorporate this in the test static lib rather than each individual binary that might need it.

Ping @levitte
OTC: This is fine for inclusion in 3.0 subject to the normal review process.
I assume @levitte has no objections regarding https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/16355#issuecomment-903097163

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.
@romen will you merge this or should I?
I was planning to do it in the weekend but I had to deal with unexpected things. I will merge it shortly as I had to squash and fix commit messages!

Merged to `master` with:

- ea1128e94e `Add tests for i2d_TYPE_fp and d2i_TYPE_fp`
- cca8a4ceda `Fix d2i_ECPKParameters_fp and i2d_ECPKParameters_fp macros`
- 7aa3dfc421 `[ec] Do not default to OPENSSL_EC_NAMED_CURVE for curves without OID`
- 78082769fa `Use applink to fix windows tests`

Thanks @t8m for the review, @bernd-edlinger to solve the Applink issue!

issue_context.title: d2i_ECPKParameters_fp throws lots of warnings
comments: @slontis could this have happened when some of the ASN1 functions were changed for constification? I think some of those were also backported to 1.1.1 and we don't have regression tests that use those functions probably!
Probably. Which is a good reason to not try fixing this type of thing later. I cant recall who added the const.

review_comments:
Shouldn't this be `&` not `==` here and throughout?

Existing code uses both forms: `==` once and `&` twice.
Uhm, this flag is actually a single bit, so there shouldn't be a difference. I can go either way. In 1.1.1 this flag is never associated with boolean operators.

I actually prefer `==`, it allows symmetry between

~~~C
if (EC_GROUP_get_asn1_flag(group) == OPENSSL_EC_NAMED_CURVE)
~~~

and 

~~~C
if (EC_GROUP_get_asn1_flag(group) == OPENSSL_EC_EXPLICIT_CURVE)
~~~

We cannot use boolean operators on `OPENSSL_EC_EXPLICIT_CURVE` as its value is `0x0`

Also, we spread around code like

~~~C
EC_GROUP_set_asn1_flag(ret_group, OPENSSL_EC_EXPLICIT_CURVE)
~~~

so I believe there is little point in overengineering for a future where this flag field will ever include additional bits: changing it in the future will break a lot of code.
If we're just using it for this one flag, the function/field names are wrong.  _named_ would make more sense.

I agree the name is not particularly friendly, especially given that other similar functions are named as `*_get_flags()` and handled with bitwise logic. "asn1_flag" is singular, but indeed not very descriptive.

It seems unfortunately it is too late to change this now. Looking back at our history, it seems quite a deliberate design the fact that this is a 1-bit flag.

Before 254ef80db19a6f6610ef07535efd699cef7aa855 it had more ~~bits~~ values —although admittedly a bit messy as it was somehow possible to be both `OPENSSL_EC_EXPLICIT` and `OPENSSL_EC_NAMED_CURVE`— and was used also to pick the default encodings for points among uncompressed, compressed and hybrid forms.
Before that we were using bitwise logic to handle the flag field, masking out bits of it in groups.
At this point it became a 1-bit field, and later on with 86f300d38540ead85543aee0cb30c32145931744, we started replacing `0` with a more descriptive `OPENSSL_EC_EXPLICIT_CURVE`.
Code expecting that field to be exactly 1-bit has now been out for so long that I am not sure we can do much about it.

Ideally we could have had this discussion much sooner, a little bit over 1 year ago when the issue was first opened, so we could have included `EC_GROUP_get_asn1_flag()` and `EC_GROUP_set_asn1_flag()` in the deprecation list for 3.0.0, while providing a new better named function as an alternative.
I don't think this is something we can do this close to beta, unfortunately, so we will likely have to stuck with it until the next major release :(

@paulidale how should I address the comment? do you still prefer bitwise access? If instead we go for `==` I'd rather do the consistency improvement of https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/16355#discussion_r691689240 as a separate PR.
Go for `==` and add the consistency separately.
